raw_response:
I will keep to the wheat-maize rotation on most of my land this year. I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so that system fits my climate, water conditions, machinery, and labor better than trying to chase novelty. At the start of the growing season, my main concern is balancing stable income with water and input costs. Winter wheat is already the backbone here, and summer maize follows it well after harvest, so I can use the full year efficiently. Because I am educated and I pay attention to management details, I will use improved or hybrid seed, keep fertilizer rates disciplined instead of excessive, irrigate only at the key stages, and rely on field scouting rather than spraying by habit. For tillage, I will use rotary tillage where I need a clean seedbed, but I will lean toward no-tillage for summer maize after wheat to save time and conserve soil moisture. My goal is not the highest possible yield on paper; it is a dependable yield with controlled cost and lower risk.
